bar: Setup as sv-5b: clean SmolLM2-135M checkpoint, the 200 TEST prompts of sv-5, 256 greedy tokens, no end-of-text stop, fp32, pinned sv-5 stack, host box1. Reference = the sv-5b box1 rows (one prompt at a time, one thread). Provider variants on box1: B8T1 = batches of 8 prompts in file order, left padding with attention mask, one thread; B1T2 = one prompt at a time, two threads; B8T2 = batches of 8, two threads. A control must hold first: the batched code path run with batch size 1 and one thread reproduces the reference tokens on the prompts it is run on (if not, the run is invalid). MET (meaning: a verifier that reruns one request at a time cannot rely on token equality when the provider batches) only if B8T1 or B8T2 differs from the reference on at least 1 of the 200 prompts. Thread effect reported with its own yes/no: B1T2 differs from the reference on at least 1 of 200. If all three are 0 of 200 the answer is no on both. Reported without a bar: first differing position and the top-1 minus top-2 margin there, number of prompts affected per variant, the same variants on box2 if run, seconds per prompt. Note: exact replay under the CIS-2 runtime is per-sequence by construction; no batched CPU implementation of it is tested here.
title: Does batching or thread count break token equality of a stock PyTorch rerun? (256 tokens, SmolLM2-135M)

ref: sv5b/long_rerun_batched.py sha256 e252843ba167de86 + jobs/sv5c.sh; feed jobs sv5c-box1 (CTRL B8T1 B1T2 B8T2) and sv5c-box2 (CTRL B8T1). Smoke on box1 before this record: batch-1 control equal to the reference on 2 prompts x 256 tokens; batch 8 on 8 prompts x 24 tokens equal to the reference prefix (nothing else seen)

summary: NOT MET (answer no on both parts): box1 B8T1, B8T2 (batches of 8, left padding) and B1T2 (2 threads) each differ from the one-at-a-time reference on 0 of 200 prompts at 256 tokens; control holds; box2 B8T1 also 0 of 200. Logit margins do shift on most steps (max 9.2e-5) but only 2 of 51,200 reference margins are below 1e-4, so the run only bounds the rate (< ~59 per million per variant); sv-5d measures it. Verified by cm-verifier with its own comparison code.
